adhered: stuck firmly to, followed strictly (a policy or rule)
advisory: giving advice rather than having power to decide
avowed: openly declared or admitted, especially a purpose or intention
abide: accept or act in accordance with (a rule or decision)
admirable: deserving respect and approval; highly praiseworthy
animated: lively, full of energy and spirit
bounden: obligatory; required by duty or moral obligation
conceded: admitted reluctantly, granted as a point or concession
conception: general idea or understanding of how something should be
consequent: following as a result or effect of something
constitutes: forms or makes up; amounts to as a whole
conviction: firm belief held strongly, especially a moral or political belief
decrees: official orders or laws issued by a ruler or authority
despatched: sent off, dispatched to a destination or for a purpose
despatches: official written reports sent by officials or diplomats
despotism: government by a single ruler with absolute, unchecked power
dwell: live in a place; or linger on and discuss a subject at length
embodying: giving concrete form to; representing an idea or principle
entail: involve or require as a necessary result or consequence
extravagance: spending money or resources wastefully, beyond what is sensible
habitat: the natural environment in which a plant or animal lives
immense: extremely large in size, amount, or degree
incredible: so remarkable it is hard to believe; astonishing
indifference: lack of interest, concern, or care about something
interfered: meddled in affairs that were not one's own business
intertribal: existing or occurring between different tribes or groups
invariably: always, on every occasion without exception
legislation: laws passed by a governing body, or the process of making them
legislative: relating to the making of laws by an elected or appointed body
littoral: the coastal strip of land lying along the shore
manifestly: clearly and obviously, in a way that is plain to see
mastery: complete control, command, or superior knowledge of something
notwithstanding: in spite of; despite the fact that
offence: wrongdoing; or an attack or aggressive action
optimism: hopefulness and confidence about future success
pacific: peaceful, not involving war or armed conflict
paralysing: rendering helpless, inactive, or unable to function properly
perseverance: persistent effort continued despite difficulty or setbacks
pioneers: early settlers or explorers who open up new territory
precipitate: hasty or rash, acting without enough thought or deliberation
precious: of great value, both monetary and personal
punitive: intended as a punishment, especially for a military or legal offence
reconcile: make compatible; bring two conflicting ideas or facts into agreement
rigidly: strictly and inflexibly, without allowing any variation
rulers: people who hold authority and govern a country or region
singularly: remarkably, in an unusual or outstanding degree
staple: a main or principal commodity produced or traded in large quantity
statesmen: experienced political leaders skilled in government and diplomacy
steamers: ships powered by steam engines, used for trade and transport
sufficiently: to a degree that is enough for a particular purpose
tenders: formal written offers to supply goods or perform work at a price
tenure: the holding of land, property, or an office for a period
traveller: a person who journeys to distant or unfamiliar places
treaties: formal written agreements between states or governments
undoubted: certain and beyond question; accepted as definitely true
unsuitable: not appropriate or fit for a particular purpose or situation
utter: complete and total; absolute in degree
whereby: by means of which; through which a process or arrangement works
unassuming: modest and not showy or self-important in manner
waste: use of resources carelessly or without purpose, leading to loss
wandering: moving about without a fixed route, roaming from place to place
phenomenon: an observable event or fact, especially one remarkable or unusual
constant: continuous or regularly repeated, happening without interruption
consequence: a result or effect following from an action or condition
gold-mining: the extraction of gold from ore, earth, or rock deposits
reproduced: copied or repeated exactly, as in a document or image
appears: seems to be the case; becomes visible or comes into existence
bringing: carrying something to a place or causing a result to happen
methods: systematic ways or procedures used to accomplish a particular task
